---
name: feedback_general-capabilities-not-specific-tools
description: When the user describes a general capability, design the general system — don't narrow to one use case and offer to build that
udc-id: ["004.8"]
arxiv-id: ["cs.MA"]
---

When the user describes a general capability ("autogenerate diagrams from relations"), design the general capability first. Don't narrow it to one specific use case (plan DAGs) and offer to build that immediately.

**Why:** The user asked about autogenerated Mermaid diagrams across the whole repo. Claude responded with a proposal to build one specific script for one specific diagram type, named it like it was the whole feature, and offered to start coding. This is two failures: (1) reducing a general capability to a specific instance, (2) jumping to build instead of thinking it through in records.

**How to apply:** When the user describes something general: think about the general pattern first. What makes it work for ANY instance, not just the most obvious one? Then express that thinking in records (plans, objectives, tasks) — not as an offer to start coding. The specific instances are examples that illustrate the general capability, not the capability itself.
